P0.3.title: Runtime config, degrade flags, logger: XTrace/relay config fails fast, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is optional and defaults flags to seeded/template
P0.3.note: The optional-key rule is load-bearing: G5 requires a green acceptance run with no API key and no network, so a fail-fast on the model key would make the gate unpassable.

P0.4.title: Relay service: seven routes incl. POST /reads/{read_id}/ingest-job, write token, exact READ_KEYS validation, server-assigned received_at, oldest_entry_age_seconds in /stats
P0.4.note: received_at and ingest_job_id are server-side metadata — a body carrying either must 400. The field is oldest_entry_age_seconds, not oldest_unverified_age: the relay tracks no verification state, and since M7 drops only verified entries, every entry still present is unverified by construction.

P0.5.title: Gate zero runner (scripts/gate0.ts, npm run gate0): N=12, two re-ingest rounds, pass = all 12 retrievable, plus DELETE + verify-gone; also measures and records SETTLE_WINDOW_SECONDS

K2.title: Off-limits matcher: isBlocked(text, topics), substring match, case- and accent-insensitive, deliberately over-blocking
K2.note: Substring, not word-boundary: a topic of 'gluten' must fire on 'glutenous'. This is the gate that stops a flagged confession being ingested anywhere ([E24]) — a false negative is a duty-of-care failure, a false positive is an annoyance. Put that reasoning in a comment so nobody 'improves' it.

K3.title: Rotation: appetite curve, half-life fit from >=3 observations else seeded median, suppressions returning reason keys not prose

K4.title: Ask scoring: plan v1.0 §3.4 verbatim, calling Cohorts.matched for pool(p); constants.ts holds KFLOOR=5 and COUNTING_K=200; stable documented tie-break
K4.note: KFLOOR is NOT in constants.ts — K6 exports it from src/kernel/cohorts.ts (privacy invariant, lives with its enforcer). Import it; do not declare a second copy. CohortStat carries no per-read signal, so compute pool(p) from the raw reads filtered by the drivers matched() returns. See DAG §4 D-5: six of eleven drivers are currently unmatchable.

M3.title: UserStore: writeProse ingests raw prose unmodified, usual/setUsual (off-limits topics live in UsualProfile), mealLog; warn when unconfirmed prose is dropped

M4.title: Relay client: typed routes incl. setJob, parseRead before sending, bounded backoff on 5xx and network only

M5.title: Approval write path + write guard: isBlocked -> mint -> parseRead -> relay, pool, setJob (best-effort), prose; blocked writes nothing anywhere
M5.note: Write ORDER is a correctness requirement: relay first, because the relay entry is the record M7 re-ingests from. Pool-first loses a read on a crash; relay-first risks only a duplicate, which K6 dedups. This isBlocked check is the authoritative one ([E24] §9 fix, covers the prose too) — L2's earlier check is an optimisation; keep both. Owns src/memory/guard.ts, which G1 tests.

M6.title: PoolView: pool union relay for a driver deduped on read_id; under pool=relay-only serve data/seeds/induction-set.json plus relay and return degraded
M6.note: Depends on S2 because the relay-only induction set is an S2 artifact.

M7.title: Settle-sweeper: verify each entry older than SETTLE_WINDOW_SECONDS, drop if retrievable, re-ingest from the entry's own six fields if not; verified-drop only, never TTL
M7.note: Two verification paths, both required (D-1): poll ingest_job_id when present, else search the pool for the read_id — setJob is best-effort so the fallback is not optional. The never-drop-unverified test is the point of this task.

S3.title: Seed loader: push generated reads to the pool scope and relay, reporting any that did not land and closing with the settle window
S3.note: XTrace has no upsert semantics, so a re-run creates duplicate pool records — K6's dedup on read_id is what keeps the census stable. Do not try to implement upsert; do warn on a detected re-run. Seeding must happen hours ahead of a demo because induction operates over the pool (design v0.8 §11).
